title: Files show as locally modified when logs says they are unchanged
body:
### What happened?

Using a send-only / receive-only folder pair set up on folders that already contained identical data, the receive folder is reporting "local additions" on about two-thirds of the files even though that is incorrect. It is not clear why this mistake is only made for some files. A spot check of several affected files indicates that they are indeed identical. Examining the Syncthing metadata for those files indicates that the blocksHash differs but it's unclear why this would be. Other metadata indicates no changes except those that could be explained by versioning (e.g. the same date appearing differently because one is in UTC and the other is in local time.)

Send folder: Windows 11 / external USB drive / NTFS / Syncthing v2.0.12

Receive folder: Ubuntu 24.04.3 / external USB drive / exFAT / Syncthing v1.27.2-ds4


This was discussed here but no outcome was reached: https://<redacted-host>/t/files-are-locally-modified-when-logs-says-they-are-unchanged/25923

### Syncthing version

v1.27.2-ds4

### Platform & operating system

Ubuntu and Windows

### Browser version

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: First of all please use 2.0 on both sides. Then please post the logs and outputs you are referring to, otherwise there is nothing to go on here.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I have updated to 2.0 and it doesn't make a difference. Rescanning does not generate any new output for the files in question and the old log is no longer available in the UI due to me upgrading.

The output is literally as above - the UI says that the receive folder has "Local Additions" when it does not, and spot-checks for the files in the list of 'additions' show that the file is identical to the one in the send folder.

If you tell me where I should look to find the logs, as generated by a default installation of Syncthing via the instructions at https://<redacted-host>/ , I will attempt to find some examples.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Syncthing cares about more things than just content of files. It cares about metadata, extended attributes, permissions etc.
exFAT doesn't handle some of the permissions etc, which get removed once synced, hence it might look like local additions etc.
To me this looks like misunderstanding how syncthing works, so suggest you continue this conversation on the forum.

Closing for now as not enough details and no clear steps to reproduce.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
The web UI only shows logs dating back to the last time it restarted / the time it was upgraded, unfortunately.

The best I can do is look at `journalctl` but that's a bit of a fire hose. After first encountering the problem I enabled a check box in the UI to see more logs, but I couldn't tell you which one that is because those checkboxes have been replaced with log-level dropdowns in the new version and they've all been reset to Info. So there is likely no useful Debug-level information after that point - I can't tell, because `journalctl` entries start 6 weeks before today and attempting to jump to the end just gets it stuck in a busy loop.

Either way, from before then, I do have hundreds, maybe thousands of instances of these Debug lines relating to a file that I know was affected (`IMG_0706.jpg`):

```
Dec 29 15:13:47 homehub syncthing[298078]: [FZL66] 2025/12/29 15:13:47.157397 set.go:268: DEBUG: zjqst-3iaxn Get(Aug 2006/IMG_0706.jpg)
Dec 29 15:13:47 homehub syncthing[298078]: [FZL66] 2025/12/29 15:13:47.157420 walk.go:405: DEBUG: walker/zjqst-3iaxn@participant5 checking: File{Name:"Aug 2006/IMG_0706.jpg", Sequence:>
Dec 29 15:13:47 homehub syncthing[298078]: [FZL66] 2025/12/29 15:13:47.157438 walk.go:416: DEBUG: walker/zjqst-3iaxn@participant5 unchanged: File{Name:"Aug 2006/IMG_0706.jpg", Sequence>
```

I have no idea what version of walk.go that relates to, but when I search that file for log lines including the term "unchanged:" it seems to imply that `curFile.IsEquivalentOptional` has returned true, which I'm _guessing_ means that a local scan has decided the file is unaltered from what's in the database.

It is this assumption which I was suggesting is inconsistent with the UI, which was telling me that, in fact, this file (and hundreds of others) was in fact 'Locally modified' and needed replacing or reverting. I never found any log that explained why these files were marked as locally modified, but everything else in the UI indicated this was the case, including both sides of the connection saying that syncing needed to take place.

The file had not been altered locally, as verified by SHA256 checks (posted on the forum), and metadata obtained for the file via the REST API seemed to show no significant differences (shown on the forum), but the blockhashes did not match. I was advised on the forum that the different versioning shouldn't result in different blockhashes, and after that there was no further suggestion for diagnostics.

After that, I posted here, was told to upgrade to version 2 on the Receive/Ubuntu side, which I did. Upon restarting, the situation was unchanged - my Receive folder was still showing that roughly 2/3rds of the files, including `IMG_0706.jpg` above, were 'Locally Modified'. After verifying that Ignore Permissions was still definitely set on both sides, I was advised to do 'a reset of Syncthings internal database'. After performing this step, the result was that Syncthing noticed that all files were unchanged (the expected result) and the problem was thereby solved.

In case it wasn't clear, the perceived bug here is "file is treated as locally modified when it is not", and that this persisted through rescans (while on v1). I mentioned logs because the logs seemed to agree that the file was unmodified and I felt this was an odd inconsistency.

It's certainly possible that the problem is confined to version 1, in which case the only major concern for modern users would probably be that a corrupt or incorrect database was not fixed during migration.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Okay, I see.

- I looked through the forum, and it shows a difference in permissions, 0644 vs 0755. That's enough to trigger the locally modified state, and not unexpected as files apparently got rescanned from being copied to a new disk with exfat or whatever. That's effectively the root cause and end of story right there as far as I can tell.
- There's discussion on the blocks hash being different, but that's irrelevant. It's computed differently between v1 and v2, but it's an entirely local attribute that's not sent over the wire and has no effect on file comparisons.
- Your log entries show the file is unchanged in that scan, which is expected as any change it saw would have picked up the first time it was scanned and stored in the database. Every scan from thereon after will show it as unchanged.

I don't think there's a bug here, sorry.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Why is the difference in permissions being treated as different files when both the send and receive were set to ignore permissions and both rescans and an upgrade took place? Are these flags not taken into account during a rescan?
